label: Third original input (t=2) when the sequence starts with f, z, n, r or o
explanation: Fires almost only at step t=2 (the third original token); 99.98% of activation mass is at t=2 and it is essentially silent in the delimiter and copy phases (22 copy-phase activations out of about 96k). Within t=2 it depends on the first original token: about 10% of t=2 steps fire when first_tok is one of f, z, n, r, o, and these account for about 98% of activation mass. Magnitude is graded by first token: strongest for f (36% of mass), then z (27%), n (20%), r (10%), o (5%). The top examples (0.867) are all f z at positions 0-1. Weak, low-quartile firing also occurs when first_tok is c, 1 or 0 (about 2% of mass). The current token at t=2 has little effect (rate is flat across in_tok), and L only matters through to_go. Dev: P=0.98, R=0.85, mass recall 0.98; most of the misses are low-quartile activations.

issues: The main claims hold up. On the dev split, t=2 holds 1.000 of activation mass. Delimiter activations are 0 and copy-phase activations are 22. Mass shares by first token are f 0.356, z 0.269, n 0.201, r 0.100 and o 0.052. Test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.985, R 0.845, F1 0.910, mass recall 0.978.

The '~10% of t=2 steps fire' figure is misstated. Steps at t=2 where the first token is in {f,z,n,r,o} make up about 5/30, roughly 17%. Each first token in that set fires at nearly 100% of its t=2 steps (for example, 16650 of 16650 for f in the dev profile). The ~0.10 numbers are rates in the prev2_tok breakdown, which also includes t != 2. In plain terms: it is 'fires at essentially every t=2 step whose first token is in the set'.

There is a systematic miss class: weak firing when the first token is c or 1 depends on the SECOND token. The explanation says only 'weak firing on c/1/0'. Taken alone, (t==2)&first_tok in {c,1,0} has test precision 0.26. Restricting it to second tokens in {z,r,o,k,h} picks out the misses (for example 'c r [u:0.20]' and 'c z [i:0.13]'). Adding that clause raises test F1 from 0.910 to 0.937, recall from 0.845 to 0.898 and mass recall to 0.990, while precision stays at 0.980. The second-token list was picked by looking at the dev split before scoring on test. The prev_tok profile is consistent with it: z, r, o, k and h are the most enriched previous tokens.

False positives (1238 on test) cluster when the first token is o (precision 0.927 when the first token is o). Several are o followed by v, t or 2, but that subset is tiny (precision 0.37, recall 0.006), so this is only minor noise.

In mass terms the gap is small: the missed class holds about 1% of mass and sits in the lowest activation quartile (test coverage of quartile 1 is 0.42). The core label is right, but the explanation leaves out that the weak tail is conditioned on the second token.
skeptic.revised_label: Third original input (t=2) when the sequence starts with f, z, n, r or o; weak firing when it starts with c or 1 and the second token is z, r, o, k or h
